title: Traffic tiling with slice affinity and autorestore for safe progressive rollouts
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: progressive rollouts frequently hit cross-slice state thrash and KV cache invalidation when small changes are routed broadly. This PR introduces traffic tiling with slice affinity and an autorestore reconciliation to contain regressions to narrowly scoped traffic tiles and automatically restore healthy routes when transient regressions resolve. Design summary: 1) Tiling engine that slices traffic by request fingerprint and route hints so user sessions are routed to a deterministic tile; 2) Slice affinity heuristics prefer colocated KV cache warm slices to reduce cold-start token overhead; 3) Autorestore controller that tracks slice health signals (latency p50/p95, error rate, inference SLO) and performs staged restores with cooldown windows and rate-limited step increases; 4) Safety gates integrated with existing rollout controller: metric gates, canary holdpoints, and manual abort signals. Implementation highlights: added a new tile reconciliation loop in services/rollout/controller/tiling_controller.go, a Python slicer library with unit tests at pkg/orchestrator/slicer.py and pkg/orchestrator/slicer_test.py, helm-configurable feature flag via charts/redwood/templates/tiling-configmap.yaml, and an e2e scenario in tests/integration/tiling_e2e.yaml that exercises partial-restore and abort scenarios. Testing and CI: unit tests added, integration e2e added; one flaky e2e test required a rerun during CI and was stabilized by adding a deterministic seed to the request generator. Migration and rollout notes: feature gated by traffic_tiling=false by default. To enable in Dedicated or Private, set tiling configmap and prewarm KV caches for low-latency slices. Rollout playbook appended to docs/rollouts/traffic-tiling-slice-affinity.md. Backwards compatibility: non-tiling routes fall through to existing routing. Related work: references ENG-7421 for slice affinity heuristics and ENG-7590 for autorestore reconciliation engine.
